summary: Backend-only tests for Telegram commission alert feature. Created safe pytest file with 12 tests: all pass. Fully mocked httpx (no outbound Telegram request), no order creation via API, no printer, no payment, no frontend action. Verified message format, endpoint composition, payload, missing-secret short-circuit, HTTP failure resilience, and _quote_or_create scheduling logic (skip test orders).
critical_code_review_comments: telegram_notifier.py is clean: no secret logging, uses env vars, graceful httpx.HTTPError handling, non-blocking via asyncio.create_task at call site.

server.py _quote_or_create correctly guards with `if not order.get('test_order')` before scheduling send_commission_alert; alert is scheduled after db.orders.insert_one, satisfying non-blocking + post-insertion requirement.

Minor: telegram_notifier catches only httpx.HTTPError. A malformed payload or unexpected transport error (e.g., asyncio.TimeoutError, RuntimeError) would still propagate to the create_task where it is swallowed by the event loop only as a warning. Consider broadening to `except Exception` for full checkout safety, though current design does not block checkout since it runs in a background task.
test_credentials: none required (all Telegram transport mocked; placeholder env values used only inside test scope via monkeypatch)
context_for_next_testing_agent: Telegram commission alert coverage lives in /app/backend/tests/test_telegram_commission_alert.py. It never hits Telegram API and never inserts orders; safe to run repeatedly. Real TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN / TELEGRAM_COMMISSION_CHAT_ID in preview env must NEVER be triggered via real order creation because a real Pi printer is connected.
